title: Quarter Circle Geometry Task Assessment
description: Show mastery by solving angle, length, and area requirements in quarter-circle designs with chords, tangents, and sectors.

questions.question: A circular design uses a 90-degree sector with radius 12 cm. What is the sector area?
questions.explanation: The sector is one-fourth of the full circle: (1/4)pi(12^2) = 36pi square centimeters.

questions.question: In a quarter-circle design, chord AB connects the endpoints of radii OA and OB. If OA = OB = 9 cm, what is AB?
questions.explanation: AB is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 9 and 9, so AB = sqrt(81 + 81) = 9sqrt(2) cm.

questions.question: If AT is tangent to the circle at A and OA is a radius, then angle OAT is 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: A radius drawn to a tangent point is perpendicular to the tangent line.

questions.question: A quarter circle has radius 10 cm. Fill in the exact area of triangle AOB formed by the two radii and the endpoint chord.
questions.explanation: Triangle AOB is right with legs 10 and 10, so its area is (1/2)(10)(10) = 50 square centimeters.

questions.question: For a quarter circle with radius 10 cm, what is the exact curved segment area between the endpoint chord and the arc?
questions.explanation: The sector area is 25pi and the triangle area is 50, so the segment area is 25pi - 50 square centimeters.

questions.question: A student says the endpoint chord in a quarter circle with radius 7 cm is 14 cm because it crosses the design. What is the best correction?
options: The chord is 7 cm because every chord equals the radius.
The chord is 7pi cm because it is part of an arc.
The chord is 7sqrt(2) cm because it is the hypotenuse of a 7-by-7 right triangle.
The chord is 49 cm because the radius must be squared.
questions.explanation: The endpoint chord is not the diameter. It is the hypotenuse of the right triangle formed by the two perpendicular radii.

questions.question: In triangle AOB from a quarter-circle endpoint chord, angle AOB = 90 degrees and OA = OB. Fill in angle OBA in degrees.
questions.explanation: The two base angles are equal and must total 90 degrees, so each is 45 degrees.

questions.question: The area of a 90-degree sector is always 90pi square units, no matter what the radius is.
questions.explanation: Sector area depends on the radius: a 90-degree sector has area (1/4)pi r^2.

questions.question: A quarter-circle tile has radius 4 cm. Which expression gives the curved segment area between the chord and the arc?
questions.explanation: The sector area is (1/4)pi(4^2) = 4pi. The triangle area is (1/2)(4)(4) = 8, so the segment area is 4pi - 8.

questions.question: A designer uses a quarter-circle sector of radius 8 cm. Set up and solve for the sector area and the endpoint chord length.
questions.correctAnswer: The sector area is (1/4)pi(8^2) = 16pi square centimeters. The endpoint chord is sqrt(8^2 + 8^2) = 8sqrt(2) centimeters.
questions.explanation: The 90-degree sector is one-fourth of the circle, and the chord is the hypotenuse of an 8-by-8 right triangle.

questions.question: Explain why the tangent requirement and the chord requirement use different relationships in a quarter-circle design.
questions.correctAnswer: The tangent requirement uses the fact that a radius to a tangent point is perpendicular to the tangent. The chord requirement uses the Pythagorean theorem because the chord is the hypotenuse of the right triangle formed by two perpendicular radii.
questions.explanation: Tangents give a perpendicular angle at the circle, while the endpoint chord length comes from the right triangle inside the sector.

questions.question: A quarter-circle sign has radius 14 cm. Which pair of measurements is correct?
options: Sector area 49pi square cm; chord 14sqrt(2) cm
Sector area 196pi square cm; chord 28 cm
Sector area 49pi square cm; chord 14 cm
Sector area 14pi square cm; chord 196 cm
questions.explanation: The sector area is (1/4)pi(14^2) = 49pi. The endpoint chord is sqrt(14^2 + 14^2) = 14sqrt(2).
